intro: Where to buy what, and whether the shop is open or closed.
p.la panadería.consejo: Many shops end in -ería: «pan» gives «panadería». It is feminine and the accent marks the í.
p.la frutería.consejo: It comes from «fruta» and also has an accent on the í: fru-te-RÍ-a. It is feminine.
p.la carnicería.consejo: It comes from «carne». In Spain c before i sounds «th»: kar-ni-the-RÍ-a.
p.la pescadería.consejo: It comes from «pescado»: la pescadería. There is often one in markets.
p.el mercado.consejo: It is masculine: «el mercado». Inside there is often a greengrocer's, butcher's and fishmonger's.
p.la librería.consejo: Careful: «librería» is the bookshop. «Library» in Spanish is «biblioteca».
p.la zapatería.consejo: It is written with z: zapato, zapatería. In Spain the z sounds «th».
p.abierto.consejo: It agrees with the noun: «el mercado está abierto», «la tienda está abierta».
p.cerrado.consejo: It is the opposite of abierto: «el bar está cerrado», «la tienda está cerrada».
p.abre.consejo: For opening times: «abre a las nueve». You ask: «¿A qué hora abre?».
p.cierra.consejo: Cerrar changes e to ie: cierro, cierras, cierra. You ask: «¿A qué hora cierra?».
p.comprar.consejo: It is a regular -ar verb: compro, compras, compra. «¿Dónde puedo comprar pan?».
p.vender.consejo: It is the opposite of comprar. The shop sells, you buy: «¿Venden pescado?».
p.necesito.consejo: It says what you lack: «Necesito pan». With a verb after it, use the infinitive.
b1.texto:
Many shops are named with **-ería**: pan → **panadería**, fruta → **frutería**, carne → **carnicería**, pescado → **pescadería**, libro → **librería**, zapato → **zapatería**.

To ask where to buy something: **¿Dónde puedo comprar pan?** To ask whether they sell something: **¿Venden pescado aquí?**

Opening hours use **abrir** and **cerrar**: **abre** a las nueve, **cierra** a las dos. A shop's state uses **estar**: **la panadería está abierta**, **el mercado está cerrado**. The adjective agrees with the shop.

Hours vary by place: check the sign on the door.
b2.f1.texto: There is a bakery on this street.
b2.f7.texto: The fish is at the fishmonger's in the market.
b4.titulo: Estar for the state, abrir for the hours
b4.texto:
There are two ways to talk about a shop:

- The **state** right now takes **estar** + adjective: **está abierta**, **está cerrado**. The adjective agrees: **la tienda abierta**, **el mercado abierto**.
- The **hours** take **abrir** or **cerrar** + time: **abre a las nueve**, **cierra a las dos**.

To say a shop exists in a place use **hay**: **Hay una librería aquí.**
b4.e2.texto: I buy books at the bookshop.
b5.f0.texto: The smell of warm bread fills the street in the morning.
b5.f1.texto: The oranges form a bright pyramid in the greengrocer's.
b5.f2.texto: The butcher cuts the meat on a thick board.
b5.f3.texto: The ice at the fishmonger's gleams under a blue lamp.
b5.f4.texto: A small bell sings above the newsstand door.
b5.f5.texto: A cool wind stirs the magazines at the newsstand.
b5.f6.texto: The market opens its big doors at eight.
b5.f7.texto: People walk slowly among the flower stalls.
b5.f8.texto: A young shop assistant arranges the shoes in a cardboard box.
b5.f9.texto: The shutters come down with a metallic noise at the end of the afternoon.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The bakery sells bread, not meat.
b6.pregunta: You need meat. Which shop do you buy it in?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: open or closed is a state and takes «estar».
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Es» does not go with a passing state like closed.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Hay» says something exists, not how it is.
b7.pregunta: Which verb says how the shop is?
b8.frase: La panadería abre a las nueve
b9.o0.refuerzo: The «a» is missing: you say «a qué hora».
b9.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «A qué hora» and the verb «abre».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Abierto» is an adjective; for opening hours you need the verb «abre».
b9.pregunta: You want to know when the shop opens. What do you ask?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the hours use the verb «abre».
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Abierta» is an adjective and does not say when it starts.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Abro» is for «yo», and here the shop is the subject.
b10.pregunta: Which verb form gives the hours?
b12.o0.refuerzo: In the library books are lent, not sold.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The «librería» is the bookshop.
b12.pregunta: You want to buy a book. Where do you go?
p.panadería.consejo: «Pan» + -ería gives a shop name. The accent on the í splits the vowels: «pa-na-de-RI-a».
p.cerrada.consejo: Feminine of «cerrado», the opposite of «abierta». The c sounds «th» and the rr is strong.
p.venden.consejo: From «vender». The v sounds like b: «BEN-den». It is the opposite of «comprar».
p.olor.consejo: The stress falls on the last syllable: «o-LOR». Be careful: it is masculine, «el olor».
p.forman.consejo: From «formar», a regular -ar verb. Stress on the first syllable: «FOR-man». «Forma» means shape.
p.pirámide.consejo: The accent mark falls on the third-to-last syllable: «pi-RA-mi-de». It looks like the English word.
p.brillante.consejo: The ll sounds like y: «bri-YAN-te». It ends in -e, so it does not change for gender.
p.carnicero.consejo: It comes from «carne». The c before e sounds «th» in Spain: «kar-ni-THE-ro».
p.tabla.consejo: Stress on the first syllable: «TA-bla». It also appears in «tabla de cortar», a chopping board.
p.gruesa.consejo: Feminine of «grueso». The «ue» is a single syllable: «GRWE-sa». The opposite is «delgada».
p.lámpara.consejo: The accent mark sits on the first syllable: «LAM-pa-ra». It looks a lot like the English word «lamp».
p.quiosco.consejo: The qu sounds like k and the u is silent: «KYOS-ko». It can also be written «kiosco».
p.revistas.consejo: The v sounds like b and the first r is strong: «rre-BIS-tas». Don't confuse it with «revisar».
p.puertas.consejo: The «ue» is one syllable: «PWER-tas». Plural of «puerta», which is feminine like «la puerta».
p.puestos.consejo: The «ue» is one syllable: «PWES-tos». Also means «position» or «job»; the sentence tells you which.
p.dependiente.consejo: With «el» it is a man; a woman is «la dependienta». Stress on «DYEN».
p.ordena.consejo: From «ordenar», related to «orden». Stress on the middle syllable: «or-DE-na».
p.cartón.consejo: The accent mark shows the stress on the last syllable: «kar-TON». The plural loses it: «cartones».
p.persianas.consejo: «ia» forms one syllable: «per-SYA-nas». Shop owners lower the «persianas» when they close.
p.bajan.consejo: From «bajar». The j sounds like a strong h: «BA-han». The opposite is «subir».
p.metálico.consejo: The accent mark falls on the third-to-last syllable: «me-TA-li-ko». It looks like the English word.
